paper_metadata.title: Parameter Setting in Quantum Approximate Optimization of Weighted Problems

summary: This paper develops parameter-setting heuristics for QAOA on weighted MaxCut, proving that for p = 1 the optimal scaling is gamma* = 1/sqrt(E[w^2](D+3)/2) for exponential weights and gamma* = 1/sqrt(E[w^2]) in the infinite-size limit, and showing that for p >= 1 the weighted objective rescales to the unweighted one by gamma -> gamma/sqrt(E[w^2]). Numerically, the proposed rules reduce the average MaxCut optimality gap to 1.1 percentage points from optimized parameters, and for portfolio optimization the rescaled xy-QAOA landscape cuts BOBYQA iterations by 7.4x on 280 instances of size 7 to 20 qubits.

experiments.description: QAOA parameter-setting study for weighted MaxCut on triangle-free regular graphs, including p=1 analytical optimization and numerical validation for p=1,2,3 on weighted graph instances.

algorithm.variant: QAOA with transverse-field mixer for weighted MaxCut parameter setting
algorithm.optimizer: local optimizer for parameter search; specific optimizer not reported for the MaxCut numerics

hyperparameters.graph_family: triangle-free (D+1)-regular graphs for theory; general weighted regular and non-regular graphs for numerics
parameter_setting_rules: gamma* = gamma_inf / sqrt((1/|E|) sum w_uv^2) * arctan(1/sqrt(D-1))
baseline from Ref. [9] using mean absolute weight

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Parameters transferred/rescaled from unweighted MaxCut infinite-size parameters; optional local optimization from those settings

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per graph vertex; binary spin variables z_u in {−1,1} encoded on qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize C(z)=1/2 sum_{(u,v) in E} w_uv (1 - z_u z_v)
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: C = 1/2 sum_{(u,v) in E} w_uv (i - Z_u Z_v)

problem_instance.description: Weighted MaxCut on triangle-free regular graphs for theory; numerical study on 34,701 weighted regular and non-regular graphs
problem_instance.dataset_name: QAOAKit weighted graph dataset from Ref. [9]

dataset_specification.description: Graphs with up to 20 nodes; weights i.i.d. from Uniform+, Uniform±, Exponential (lambda=0.2), and Cauchy distributions

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical comparison of approximation ratios and optimality gaps against optimized parameters and prior parameter-setting method; results aggregated over the dataset and across p values

implementation_details.classical_solver: local optimizer; BOBYQA mentioned only for portfolio experiment, not this MaxCut study
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Rescale edge weights by sqrt((1/|E|) sum w_uv^2) before applying unweighted MaxCut parameter rules
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute approximation ratios and optimality gaps

speedup_claims.conditions: across all graphs, p values, and edge-weight distributions in the numerical study
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a reduction in optimality gap, not a runtime speedup.
Reported as disparity from optimized parameters, not computational speed.

speedup_claims.conditions: weighted MaxCut on large-girth regular graphs, p >= 1
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a parameter-scaling rule, not a speedup claim.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QAOA parameter scaling gamma = Theta(D^-1/2) for p=1; landscape correspondence for p>=1 under rescaling

experiments.description: QAOA applied to portfolio optimization with a budget constraint using an xy Hamming-weight-preserving mixer, comparing original vs rescaled objective landscapes and optimizer convergence.

algorithm.variant: xy-QAOA (QAOA with xy mixer for constrained portfolio optimization)

hyperparameters.initial_state: uniform superposition over all Hamming-weight k states (Dicke state)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Started from optimal QAOA parameters for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model: gamma_init = 1, beta_init = pi/4

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per asset; binary variable x_j indicates whether asset j is selected
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T Sigma x - mu^T x subject to sum_j x_j = k
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraint enforced by xy mixer and Dicke-state initial state

problem_instance.description: Random portfolio optimization instances with budget constraint

dataset_specification.description: 280 instances total; 20 instances for each qubit count between 7 and 20

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Random instances generated in qiskit finance; objective reformulated in spin variables and rescaled by coefficient computed separately for each instance; q=0.5 and k=floor(n/2)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: BOBYQA local optimization from fixed initial point; compare original vs rescaled objective; report performance profiles and fraction of instances solved

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Reformulate portfolio problem in spin variables; rescale objective using coefficient from Eq. (8), including linear terms mu_j
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare convergence to same optimum; compute performance profiles and iteration counts

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Rescaled landscape easier to optimize; original landscape flat

speedup_claims.conditions: 280 random portfolio instances, 7 to 20 qubits, p=1, xy mixer, fixed initial point
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a classical optimizer convergence improvement, not a quantum runtime speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not applicable; the experiment evaluates optimizer convergence on 280 simulated portfolio instances of size 7 to 20 qubits.

Improvement is in optimizer iterations, not end-to-end quantum advantage
